title: Minimum output on private (MEV-routed) sells

options.name: Keep current behaviour: every private sell (full, partial, every reason) uses amountOutMin = 0
options.risk: A sell accepts any output: price movement between trigger and inclusion, a sell tax raised by the token owner, or a chain where the private route is a plain sequencer submission (Base, Arbitrum) can turn the exit into a near-zero fill (AUD-EXIT-001). The loss is bounded by the position.

options.name: Bounded floor on every private sell, from a fresh quote with the reason-aware slippage (the computePublicMinOut rule the public fallback already uses)
options.behavior_impact: Private sells revert instead of filling below the floor; the ladder then falls through to the public fallback.
options.risk: During a fast rug a floor can make the private attempt revert and cost its confirm window before the public fallback runs; the quote itself has the probe problems of AUD-EXIT-003 unless it is a proper sell quote for the held amount.

options.name: Bounded floor for routine exits (trailing, stop-loss, urgency, partial); keep 0 for anti-rug exits only
options.behavior_impact: Routine exits gain a floor; anti-rug exits keep filling at any price to get out first.
options.risk: Anti-rug sells keep the zero-floor exposure; a mislabelled reason would pick the wrong policy.

recommendation: bounded-routine-zero-antirug (the research recommendation), decided only after a Phase 23 fork replay of the LADYS position and rug fixtures shows the anti-rug private attempt still lands; the quote used for the floor must be a sell quote for the held amount, not the price probe.
default: Keep current behaviour until the owning phase decides (milestone contract). This card covers S1 capital findings, which cannot rest on the default: until it is decided and fixed it blocks the live re-entry gate.
behavior_impact: Decides whether an exit sell can ever fill at any price.
needed_by: Phase 24 discussion (capital fixes, after the Phase 23 real-path proof)
